section_summary: This section contains agreements licensing industrial processes and patents to Japanese companies, including ammonia synthesis, electrode coke production, sulfuric acid production, and the magnetic material Sendust. The agreements set production capacities, royalties, payment terms, technical assistance, and territorial rights. The section opens with the end of an earlier agreement and closes before the Sendust agreement ends.

subfiles.title: Montecatini–Dai Nippon Jinzohiryo 1926 agreement and patent licence schedules
subfiles.doc_type: agreement, licence forms and patent schedule
subfiles.from: Montecatini Società Generale per l'Industria Mineraria ed Agricola
subfiles.about: Licensing the Fauser process and associated patents for chemical production in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The surviving pages finish provisions for a joint company's reserves, dividends, employee benefits and Montecatini royalties. They then set out patent licence forms granting Dai Nippon rights in Japan and other territories, with terms for patent protection and renewal. A schedule lists patents and applications concerning synthetic ammonia, electrolysis, nitrogen recovery and nitric acid.

subfiles.title: Cover sheet for Montecatini–Dai Nippon agreement
subfiles.about: Identifying the following agreement between Montecatini and Dai Nippon.
subfiles.summary: Cover sheet dates the Montecatini–Dai Nippon agreement and names Bryden & Williams.

subfiles.title: Montecatini–Dai Nippon Fauser process agreement
subfiles.from: Montecatini Società Generale per l'Industria Mineraria ed Agricola
subfiles.about: Revising exclusive Japanese rights, plant expansion commitments, and payments under the 1926 Fauser process agreement.
subfiles.summary: Dai Nippon undertakes to increase nitrogen production capacity while Montecatini confirms its exclusive licence in the Japanese zone. The agreement revises capital payments and production royalties by capacity band, sets deadlines and minimum royalties, and permits sub-concessions. It addresses delayed construction, loss of exclusivity following non-payment, and the meaning of subsidiary companies.

subfiles.title: Montecatini–Dai Nippon compromise agreement
subfiles.from: Montecatini Società Generale per l'Industria Mineraria ed Agricola
subfiles.about: Settling a dispute over interpretation of the 1929 Fauser process agreement.
subfiles.summary: The parties define Dai Nippon's capacity separately from that of independent sub-concessionaires and revise capital and production royalty obligations. Dai Nippon undertakes to arrange a new plant of at least 10,000 tons annual nitrogen capacity, with specified payment, guarantee and construction terms. The agreement confirms exclusive Japanese rights while payments continue, provides authority to enforce patents and grant sub-licences, and retains the earlier agreements where unmodified.

subfiles.title: Koppers–Nippon Keikinzoku electrode coke plant agreement
subfiles.from: Heinrich Koppers Gesellschaft mit beschränkter Haftung
subfiles.about: Providing the Koppers system, designs and assistance for electrode coke plants in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Koppers agrees to supply drawings, specifications and operating assistance for plants with a combined annual capacity of 50,000 metric tons of electrode pitch coke and petroleum coke. The agreement specifies equipment, delivery schedules, payments in Reichsmarks, confidentiality and limits on transferring or extending the licence. Its effectiveness depends on Japanese government approval of foreign exchange payments. The date is supplied by the later agreement identifying this as the original agreement.

subfiles.title: Cover for Lurgi sulfuric acid contact plant agreement
subfiles.about: Identifying an agreement for a Lurgi sulfuric acid plant and hot and cold Cottrell equipment.
subfiles.summary: Title page identifies the plant and associated Cottrell equipment.

subfiles.title: Lurgi–Nippon Kogyo sulfuric acid contact plant agreement
subfiles.from: Lurgi Gesellschaft für Chemie und Hüttenwesen m.b.H.
subfiles.about: Licensing and supplying a 100-ton-per-day sulfuric acid plant at Hitachi.
subfiles.summary: Lurgi grants a contact process licence and undertakes to supply drawings, vanadium contact mass, and hot and cold Cottrell equipment. The agreement sets delivery dates, a performance guarantee, a lump-sum price, staged payments, confidentiality, engineering assistance and arbitration. The opening gives 15 June 1939, while the closing reads 7 July 1937; the dates conflict in the OCR.

subfiles.title: Koppers–Keikinzoku–Pitch-Coke Kogyo transfer and expansion agreement
subfiles.from: Heinrich Koppers Gesellschaft mit beschränkter Haftung; Nippon Keikinzoku Kabushiki Kaisha
subfiles.about: Transferring and expanding rights under the 1940 Koppers electrode coke agreement.
subfiles.summary: The parties transfer obligations for the original coke plants to Pitch-Coke Kogyo and change both to pitch coke production, totaling 50,000 metric tons annually. They provide separate rights and payment schedules for Keikinzoku's petroleum coke plant and an additional Pitch-Coke Kogyo plant. The agreement permits construction across specified Japanese and Asian territories and sets terms for later expansion and notice of competing orders.

subfiles.title: Sumitomo–German Group Sendust patent licence agreement
subfiles.to: Allgemeine Elektricitäts-Gesellschaft; Felten & Guilleaume Carlswerk Aktiengesellschaft; Siemens & Halske Aktiengesellschaft
subfiles.about: Granting the German companies exclusive rights to manufacture and sublicense Sendust under specified patents.
subfiles.summary: The German-language agreement lists Sendust patent rights and grants the German companies an exclusive licence across specified territories, with rights to sublicense in Europe. Sumitomo undertakes to provide manufacturing instructions, improvements and potentially an experienced engineer. The agreement sets percentage royalties, a minimum annual payment, accounting and patent maintenance duties. Its commencement depends on a German patent grant; the text continues beyond page 446.
